designs.title: Probably Fine
designs.why: Tight, consistent icon set with a matched condensed label face and a confident headline; the deadpan joke reads instantly and the grid holds together as one block at distance. But in one ink nothing actually looks 'lit' - it reads as a reference chart from a manual, not a dashboard on fire, so the punchline does half the work alone. A few glyphs are weak (coolant reads as a key, airbag figure is clumsy).
designs.fix: Make the lights read as ON: add short glow/radiating ticks around each icon (or set them in a dashboard-cluster silhouette) so the image itself says 'everything is lit' before PROBABLY FINE lands.

designs.title: How to Go to Bed
designs.why: Best of the three: loose brush drawings with real personality, a quiet serif title, and the repeated 'Turn around.' is a genuine comic rhythm that rewards a second look; 'Sigh.' is a perfect ending. Weak spots are execution: steps 4 and 5 have tangled, hard-to-read anatomy, and on the tee the thin lines and small italic captions make the whole thing look faint and undersized.
designs.fix: Redraw steps 4-5 so each pose is a clean readable silhouette mid-spin, and bump brush weight and caption size about 30% so it holds up as a back print.

designs.title: The Box
designs.why: Skilled, clean inking and the tabby has real charm, but the gag is the most familiar cat joke there is and the storytelling is soft: panels 1 and 2 are both 'hands holding the bed', and the box vanishes in panel 2 so the payoff is not set up. Fine whisker and stripe hatching risks filling in at print size, and the bed breaking out of panel 3 looks accidental rather than designed.
designs.fix: Rework panel 2: bed placed on the floor, cat turning its back on it and eyeing the empty box, so the three beats read as setup-snub-payoff without repeating the hands.
